The number of promises that are waiting to run (i.e. their internal `fn` was not called yet).

### limit.clearQueue()

Discard pending promises that are waiting to run.

This might be useful if you want to tear down the queue at the end of your program's lifecycle or discard any function calls referencing an intermediary state of your app.

Note: This does not cancel promises that are already running.

When `rejectOnClear` is enabled, pending promises are rejected with an `AbortError`.
This is recommended if you await the returned promises, for example with `Promise.all`, so pending tasks do not remain unresolved after `clearQueue()`.

### limit.concurrency

Get or set the concurrency limit.

### limitFunction(fn, options) <sup>named export</sup>

Returns a function with limited concurrency.

The returned function manages its own concurrent executions, allowing you to call it multiple times without exceeding the specified concurrency limit.

Ideal for scenarios where you need to control the number of simultaneous executions of a single function, rather than managing concurrency across multiple functions.

import {limitFunction} from 'p-limit';

const limitedFunction = limitFunction(async () => {

name: limit_function_type_contract
description: p-limit declares limitFunction's returned wrapper type as Pick<LimitFunction, 'clearQueue' | 'onIdle'>
type: project
---
p-limit's `limitFunction` public type contract, as declared in `index.d.ts`. It is a declared type-level restriction, not runtime enforcement.

Input: `function_: (...arguments_: Arguments) => PromiseLike<ReturnType>` plus a required `options: Options` (`readonly concurrency: number;` and `readonly rejectOnClear?: boolean;`). Unlike the default export's `pLimit(concurrency: number | Options)`, and unlike `LimitFunction`'s own call signature, whose function parameter is declared `(...arguments_: Arguments) => PromiseLike<ReturnType> | ReturnType`, the declared `limitFunction` input is PromiseLike-returning; PromiseLike and Promise are distinct type-level contracts.

Output: the declared return type changed from `((...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>) & Pick<LimitFunction, 'clearQueue'>;` to `((...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>) & Pick<LimitFunction, 'clearQueue' | 'onIdle'>;` — the wrapper is still declared to preserve the argument tuple and return `Promise<ReturnType>`, and its declared extra `LimitFunction` members are `clearQueue` and `onIdle` rather than the earlier `clearQueue` alone, still not `activeCount`, `pendingCount`, `concurrency` or `map`.

In `index.js` the wrapper's `clearQueue` came from `Object.defineProperty(limitedFunction, 'clearQueue', {value: limit.clearQueue,});`; this run added `Object.defineProperty(limitedFunction, 'onIdle', {value: limit.onIdle,});`. An ad-hoc `node -e` probe printed `limitFunction onIdle ok` after awaiting two wrapper `onIdle()` calls.

newMemories.content:
---
description: p-limit's onIdle() gates on the added isIdle predicate `activeCount === 0 && queue.size === 0`
type: project
---
This run added an `onIdle` property to p-limit's limiter in `index.js` and declared it in `index.d.ts` as `onIdle: () => Promise<void>;`. Its body returns `Promise.resolve()` when `isIdle()` holds, otherwise it registers the promise's `resolve` in the shared `idleWaiters` array (`idleWaiters.push(resolve);`), so multiple concurrent waiters are supported and are drained by `checkIfIdle()` with `while (idleWaiters.length > 0) { idleWaiters.shift()(); }`.

Idleness is declared as `const isIdle = () => activeCount === 0 && queue.size === 0;`. `activeCount` is incremented inside `resumeNext()` (`activeCount++; queue.dequeue().run();`) and decremented only in `next()`, which `run()` calls after `await result;`, so a reserved slot counts as work and a job whose result promise never settles keeps its `onIdle()` waiter unresolved. In `run()`, `checkIfIdle()` is called only after `next()` has already had the chance to re-arm a slot via `resumeNext()`. `checkIfIdle()` is also called in both `clearQueue()` branches — after `queue.clear()` when `rejectOnClear` is falsy, and after the dequeue-and-reject loop when `rejectOnClear` is set — so waiters are released when the discarded queue empties and no job is active.

Observed ad-hoc `node -e` probe output (not the project test suite): `before resolve false`, `idle after resolve ok`, `already idle true`, `rejected job idle ok`, `rejectOnClear idle ok`, `reserved activeCount 1`, `enqueue-on-resolve not early idle false`, `clearQueue releases waiters true`, and `await queued? Promise { <pending> }` for a discarded queued promise under the default `rejectOnClear: false`.
